allies.rationale_text: Resilience gives internal-locus-of-control a practical recovery frame by keeping focus on controllable responses to setbacks.
allies.source_quote: Resilience is strongly linked to this internal focus
allies.affinity_rationale: Internal LOC's agency principle requires self-discipline and managing the emotional self — resilience provides the persistence mechanism that sustains agency through adversity.
allies.activation_condition: When maintaining a sense of personal agency requires bouncing back from setbacks rather than ceding control to external circumstances

allies.rationale_text: Systems-thinking helps internal-locus-of-control distinguish between agency and the system structure that must be redesigned.
allies.source_quote: viewing the organization as a machine
allies.affinity_rationale: Internal LOC provides the 'necessary motivation (agency) to fix faulty systems' while systems thinking provides 'the map necessary to identify the high-leverage points within the system that are actually controllable' — agency plus map.
allies.activation_condition: When personal agency needs to be directed at the right leverage points within a complex system rather than wasted on uncontrollable variables

antagonists.rationale_text: System-1 undermines internal-locus-of-control by allowing the emotional lower-level brain to override conscious agency, making chemical choices that protect the self before the deliberate mind can intervene.
antagonists.source_quote: Internal LOC requires the logical, higher-level self to manage the emotional, lower-level self (the two yous). Conflict arises because the emotional part often resists necessary self-discipline or painful truths.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: The 'emotional brain system constantly shapes 90-95% of our decisions nonconsciously' — System 1 undermines the conscious, deliberate control that internal LOC demands.
antagonists.activation_condition: When automatic emotional reactions override the deliberate, conscious agency that internal locus of control requires for effective self-directed action

antagonists.rationale_text: Optimism-bias undermines internal-locus-of-control by inflating the sense of personal causation, leading to false confidence that spins better narratives rather than discovering what is actually within one's influence.
antagonists.source_quote: False Confidence: Motivated reasoning (processing information to get a desired conclusion rather than discovering truth). Being smart can worsen this bias by allowing for better narrative spinning.
antagonists.affinity_rationale: Internal LOC can produce false confidence through motivated reasoning — overestimating what is controllable when optimism inflates perceived agency beyond reality.
antagonists.activation_condition: When a strong sense of personal agency leads to overestimating control over outcomes that are actually driven by external or systemic factors

structured_tensions.tension_text: Internal-locus-of-control conflicts with status-quo-bias when agency is ceded to default environmental inertia.
Internal-locus-of-control conflicts with commitment-bias when prior identity commitments block corrective action.
Internal-locus-of-control conflicts with confirmation-bias when feedback is processed to protect the sense of control instead of revising it.
